prompt: A printable US Letter portrait page (8.5 by 11 inches) for a kids' pretend-play game, drawn flat and straight-on and filling the whole image: the page itself, not a photo or mockup of paper. Plain white paper with a clean white margin of about half an inch on every side where nothing is drawn, so it prints on a home printer. The game is "Cozy Café". Art style for the whole kit: bright, friendly flat vector cartoon like a modern kids' picture-book app: bold clean dark purple outlines, flat cheerful fills in coral red, sunny yellow, lime green, sky blue, deep purple and cream, soft rounded shapes, no gradients, no shading texture, no photo effects, lots of white paper. Ink-friendly: color sits on white, no full-page dark background. Draw ONE menu card for a pretend restaurant that fills the page inside the margin: a decorative themed frame (little forks, spoons, hearts, checkered corners). At the top the restaurant name "Cozy Café" and under it the big word "Menu". Then 4 rows, one dish per row, evenly spaced, with a dotted leader between dish and price: "Pancakes" with a small picture of a stack of pancakes on the left and the price "$3" on the right; "Pizza" with a small picture of a slice of pizza on the left and the price "$4" on the right; "Soup" with a small picture of a bowl of soup on the left and the price "$2" on the right; "Cupcake" with a small picture of a cupcake on the left and the price "$1" on the right. The ONLY words on the page, spelled exactly letter for letter: "Cozy Café", "Menu", "Pancakes", "Pizza", "Soup", "Cupcake", "$3", "$4", "$2", "$1". Big, clear, rounded print letters, easy for a 5-year-old to read, dark on a light background, never curved along a path, never tiny. No other words, letters, numbers or signatures anywhere. Kid-friendly and gentle, for ages 4 to 8: no guns, no knives, no real weapons (a toy sword is fine), no blood, nothing scary, no real people, no brands, no logos.
